status_note: Reproduces on Snowflake 10.40.102. `SUBSTR`'s docs take the start and length as integers without a range (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/substr); `POSITION` with a start past 2^31 raises `out of range`, so the two disagree. Not searched in Snowflake's community forum yet.
summary: `SUBSTR` reads its start and length as 32-bit integers and wraps larger values silently: a start of 2^32 + 2 is 2, a start of 2^32 - 1 is -1 (counted from the end), and a length of 2^31 or 3·10^9 is negative, so the result is `''`. A `BIGINT` position computed from data can thus pick the wrong characters with no error.
handling: sverify's SQL (`SnowflakeDialect.substring`) clamps starts and lengths to 2^31 - 1, past the end of any string (at most 128 MiB), raises for a start of 2^32 or more as the reference does, and refuses a literal length of 2^32 or more.
